about.title: Banning Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Riverside County residents in Banning rely on local clinics, urgent care centers, and hospitals for care they trust to be careful and competent. When a diagnosis is missed, a surgery goes sideways, or medication is mishandled, the harm can follow a patient for years. Medical malpractice cases are different from other injury claims — California requires a qualified medical expert to review the care and confirm it fell below the accepted standard, since a bad outcome by itself doesn't prove malpractice. Strict notice periods and filing deadlines also apply, so early action matters. LawProactive doesn't practice law or take a cut of any recovery; we simply connect Banning residents with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless money is recovered. If something felt wrong about your care, it's worth having someone qualified take a closer look.

items.title: Understanding MICRA's Deadlines
items.desc: California generally gives one year from when you discover the harm, and no more than three years from the injury itself, to bring a claim. An independent attorney can help track these dates before they slip by.

items.title: Meeting the 90-Day Notice Rule
items.desc: Before filing suit against a healthcare provider, California law usually requires 90 days' advance notice. Missing this step can delay or derail a claim, so early guidance matters.

items.title: Navigating Expert Review Requirements
items.desc: Because a qualified medical expert almost always has to confirm the standard of care was breached, connecting with an attorney who works with such experts is essential to building a credible case.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a medical malpractice claim in Banning?
items.answer: California generally allows one year from when you discover the injury, capped at three years from when it happened. Because these windows can be shorter than they sound, especially with the required 90-day pre-suit notice, it's wise to speak with an attorney soon after you suspect something went wrong.

items.question: Is every bad medical outcome considered malpractice?
items.answer: No. California law recognizes that medicine involves risk, and an unfavorable result alone doesn't prove negligence. A claim typically requires a qualified medical expert to show the care fell below the accepted standard.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney in Banning?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and the independent attorneys in our network handle malpractice cases on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no upfront cost to have your situation reviewed.
